body.p: Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application in view of the foregoing amendments and following remarks. Status of the Claims
Claims 1-11 are pending in this application and stand rejected. By this amendment, claim
1 is amended. New claims 12-16 are added. No new matter has been added by this amendment. Allowable Subject Matter
Claims 3-5 are indicated as allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.
Applicant appreciates the Examiner's indication of allowability. Rejections under 35 U.S.C. $112

Claims 1-11 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) allegedly being indefinite. Specifically, the Office Action indicates that the phrase "such as" of claim 1 renders the claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following the phrase are part of (or excluded from) the claimed invention.

In response, relevant portion of claim 1 has been amended to recite, for example, "without using a driving mechanism including such as a belt for transmitting a driving force," thereby clarifying the unclearness. Supports for the amendments may be found, for example, at paragraphs [0031] and [0035] of the specification as originally filed.
In view of the above, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections of claims 1-11 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) is respectfully requested. Rejections under 35 U.S.C. {{ 102&103
Claims 1, 6-7 and 11 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1)/(a)(2) as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent No. 6,485,250 ("Hofmeister").
Claim 2 has been rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Hofmeister in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2003/0011338 Al ("Gilchrist").
Claims 8-10 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Hofmeister in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2022/0131452 ("Kojima").

In rejecting independent claim 1, the Office Action indicates that Hofmeister discloses each and every element of claim 1. Specifically, the Office Action equates, among others, the "inner arms 72, 78," "motors 42, 44, 46" and "frame 32" of Hofmeister to "a plurality of hands," "a plurality of hand drive motors" and "arm" of claim 1 of the instant application, respectively. Moreover, the Office Action equates the "center axis D" of Hofmeister to both the "pivoting axis" and "motor axis" of claim 1 of the instant application. [Office Action, page 3]
Moreover, in Response to Arguments section, the Office Action indicates that:

the claimed hands are now being interpreted as elements 72 and 78 in the Hofmeister reference, while element 32 is considered the arm. As the hands of Hofmeister pivot about the same axis D as the central axis of the motors under the driving force of the motors, without the use of any belts, it is considered to meet the broadest reasonable interpretation of "configured to directly drive the plurality of hands, respectively, without using a mechanism such as a belt for transmitting a driving force". It is also noted that the claimed "a driving force" is considered the force to
drive elements 72 and 78 about Axis D.
[Office Action, page 6]
Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Examiner's rejection rationales as indicated above. For example, Applicant notes that, for example, col. 6, lines 9-14 of Hofmeister describe that:
The first motor 42 is used in conjunction with the two other motors 44, 46 in order to rotate the entire arm assembly 36 about the main axis D.

The first motor 42 is rotated to rotate the middle shaft 50a and, thus, rotate the main pulley 70. The motors 44, 46 are moved in the same direction and speed as the motor 42 to rotate the inner arms 72, 78 with
the pulley 70.
[Emphasis added]

That is, referring to FIGS. 3 and 3A of Hofmeister as reproduced below, Applicant notes that the alleged plurality of hand drive motors (e.g., motors 42, 44, 46 of Hofmeister) merely drive the alleged plurality of hands (e.g., inner arms 72, 78 of Hofmeister) with the pulley 70 (i.e., via or using the pulley 70). However, Applicant notes that the alleged plurality of hand drive motors (e.g., motors 42, 44, 46 of Hofmeister) does NOT directly drive the alleged plurality of hands (e.g., inner arms 72, 78 of Hofmeister). As a result, Applicant believes that Hofmeister fails to disclose "a plurality of hand drive motors arranged ..., and configured to directly drive the plurality of hands, respectively, without using a mechanism ...," as specifically recited in claim 1. [Emphasis added]
Applicant believes that Hofmeister fails to disclose each and every element of claim 1 for at least the reason set forth above.
Nonetheless, in an effort to expedite the prosecution process, independent claim 1 has been amended for further clarification. In particular, amended claim 1 recites, inter alia,:
a plurality of hand drive motors arranged in a direction along the pivoting
axis, such that a motor axis ... concentric with the pivoting axis, ...; and
an arm extending in a direction perpendicular to the pivoting axis and
including therein the plurality of hand drive motors.
[Emphasis added]
Supports for the amendments may be found, for example, at paragraph [0026] along with FIG. 1 of the specification as originally filed.

Applicant believes that amended claim 1 reciting the specific feature further distinguishes over Hofmeister. For example, Applicant notes that the alleged arm (e.g., frame 32 of Hofmeister) extends in a direction parallel to the alleged pivoting axis or motor axis (e.g., center axis D of Hofmeister), but does NOT extend in a direction perpendicular to the alleged pivoting axis or motor axis (e.g., center axis D of Hofmeister).
As Applicants understand it, the secondary references including Gilchrist and Kojima fail to show or suggest the features of amended claim 1 discussed above.

In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 as amended is neither anticipated by nor rendered obvious in view of the references cited by the Examiner (i.e., Hofmeister, Gilchrist and Kojima), either taken alone or in combination, for at least the reason discussed above.
Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1)/(a)(2) is respectfully requested.

Applicant has chosen in the interest of expediting prosecution of this patent application to distinguish the cited documents from the pending claims as set forth above. However, these statements should not be regarded in any way as admissions that the cited documents are, in fact, prior art. Also, Applicant has not individually addressed the rejections of the dependent claims because Applicant submits that the independent claim (i.e., claim 1) from which they respectively
depend is in condition for allowance as set forth above. Applicant however reserves the right to address such rejections of the dependent claims should such be necessary. New claims

New claims 12-16 have been added to recite the invention in an alternative manner. Specifically, new claims 12 and 13 in depending from one of claims 1 and 11 is also believed allowable for at least the similar reason for amended claim 1 discussed above. Supports for the new claims may be found, for example, at paragraph [0027] along with FIG. 1 of the original specification.

Moreover, Applicant believes that new independent claim 14 reciting the allowable feature of claim 3, and new claim 15 in depending from claim 14 are also allowable for at least the reasons set forth in the Office Action. Moreover, Applicant believes that new independent claim 16 reciting the allowable feature of claim 5 is also allowable for at least the reasons set forth in the Office Action.
Applicant believes that the application as amended including the new claims is in condition for allowance and such action is respectfully requested.

No petitions or additional fees are believed due for this amendment and/or any accompanying submissions. However, to the extent that any additional fees and/or petition is required, including a petition for extension of time, Applicant hereby petitions the Commissioner to grant such petition, and hereby authorizes the Commissioner to charge any additional fees, including any fees which may be required for such petition, or credit any overpayment to Deposit Account No. 604,560.
Please contact the undersigned for any reason. Applicant seeks to cooperate with the Examiner including via telephone if convenient for the Examiner.
An early and favorable examination on the merits is respectfully requested.
